about.pageDescription: Learn about the Open Helplines project, its data, and how to contribute.
about.title: About Open Helplines
about.whatIsThisText1: Open Helplines is a free, open-source dataset of mental health and crisis support helplines from around the world. The data is structured, machine-readable, and released under the {cc0link} (Public Domain) license — meaning you can use it for any purpose, including commercial, without attribution.
about.whatIsThisText2: This visualization site helps explore the coverage and characteristics of global crisis support resources.
dataItems: Each helpline includes phone/text/chat contacts, languages, and operating hours
Categories: suicide prevention, mental health, crisis, domestic violence, LGBTQ+, and more
Data is verified periodically and community-maintained
Available in JSON format, compatible with the open-helplines npm package
about.contributeText: We welcome contributions of helpline data from any country. If you know of a crisis support resource not in our database, please open a pull request or issue on GitHub.
about.licenseDataText: CC0 1.0 Universal — No rights reserved. Use freely for any purpose.

contribute.pageDescription: How to contribute helpline data to the Open Helplines project.
contribute.title: Contribute Data
contribute.subtitle: Help us build the most comprehensive open directory of crisis support resources.
howToSteps: Find or create the file at {filePath}
Add your helpline using the JSON schema format (see example below)
Open a pull request — we review and merge quickly
guidelines: One helpline per record (no aggregated listings)
Verify phone numbers and URLs before submitting
Include accurate operating hours (24/7 or specific times)
Data must be factual and verifiable — no promotional content

private.whyPageTitle: Why this page is private — Crisis Finder
private.whyPageDescription: Technical explanation of the privacy guarantees for the No-Log Crisis Finder.
private.whyPageSubtitle: A transparent explanation of the technical measures that make this crisis finder genuinely privacy-preserving.
private.whySection1Body: Open Helplines is built with Next.js static export (output: 'export') and served from GitHub Pages. There is no application server that receives your search query. Every page is pre-built HTML/JS/CSS served from a CDN. The only server involved is GitHub's CDN, which receives a standard HTTP request log — it never sees your search query because search state stays in the browser.
private.whySection2Body: A Content-Security-Policy meta tag is embedded in every page. It blocks connections to Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, Mixpanel, Hotjar, Segment, and any other third-party tracking endpoint. The only permitted external connection is nominatim.openstreetmap.org, used only when you explicitly grant geolocation access in the emergency banner.
private.whySection3Body: When you click a helpline link, the destination website normally receives a Referer header showing where you came from. This page sets referrerPolicy="no-referrer" on every external link, and a global <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer"> tag. The helpline website sees no information about where you came from.
private.whySection4Title: Ephemeral state — nothing written to storage
private.whySection4Body: All search filters (country, method, text query) are held in React component state. When you navigate away or close the tab, the state is garbage-collected. No write ever occurs to localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, IndexedDB, or any other persistent browser storage. The URL bar is never updated with your query.

donate.pageDescription: Support the mental health helplines and crisis services that save lives around the world.
donate.title: Support Mental Health Helplines
donate.subtitle: Every call answered is a life that matters. The helplines in this registry are run by volunteers and non-profits that rely on your support.
donate.whyText: Crisis helplines operate 24/7 on tight budgets. A single call can take 45 minutes of a trained volunteer's time. Your donation helps keep lines open, trains more counsellors, and expands language support.
donate.helplinesSubtext: These organisations have public donation pages. 100% of your donation goes directly to the helpline.
donate.projectText: Open Helplines is a free, open-source dataset maintained by volunteers. If you find it useful, consider starring the repository or sponsoring the maintainers.
